recipes.name: Bow Tie Pasta Salad
ingredients_raw: 1 (10 ounce) basket cherry or grape tomatoes
2 cups creamy salad dressing (such as Miracle Whip®)

steps.text: Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a rolling boil. Cook bow tie pasta at a boil until tender yet firm to the bite, about 12 minutes; drain. Quickly rinse the cooked pasta in cold water to stop it from continuing to cook; drain.
Mix cooled pasta, broccoli, tomatoes, sliced green onions, celery, red bell pepper, and green bell pepper in a large bowl.
Gently stir salad dressing and Parmesan cheese together in a bowl until evenly mixed; season to taste with sugar, basil, and salt.
Pour salad dressing mixture over pasta mixture; gently toss to coat evenly.
For best results, chill salad in refrigerator before serving to allow flavors to blend.

raw_recipe.headline: Bow Tie Pasta Salad
raw_recipe.description: This bow tie pasta salad with farfalle pasta, broccoli, celery, and bell pepper is tossed with a deliciously creamy Parmesan and basil salad dressing.

review.reviewBody: As is, three stars == too sweet! I'd omit the sugar and toss the broccoli in with the pasta about three minutes before done to "shock" the broccoli so it keeps its crunch and bright green color -- five stars. Also good if you substitute the green onions with diced sweet or red onions. For a full meal, I add leftover cooked chicken or ham.

I used broccolini and dunked it in the pasta water as it was cooking for a few seconds before I cut it up. I also didn't add the sugar but did add a little bit of mustard. Very refreshing pasta salad!

The best pasta salad I have had in years! My son is a very picky eater, but tends to love pasta. He loved this as well. My kids love veggies, but not raw ones, so I did omit the celery and green pepper, but I figured because red peppers tend to be sweet that they would be fine. I added them, but minced. Also, I used frozen broccoli and added to the pasta about 3 minutes before it was done boiling. I will definitely make for every bbq and will even make for a week night meal using chopped chicken, smoked sausage, or italian sausage. The possibilities are endless. EXCELLENT RECIPE!

Beautiful presentation for my recent potluck dinner- and absolutely delicious!! I substituted fresh chopped baby spinach for the red pepper. I used half the sugar because I could not imagine 1/4 cup in a pasta salad. Great leftovers- was just as beautiful and delicious on day 2.. The veggies started to look tired on day 3, but still tasted great. Can't wait to make this again!

I bet this would be tasty with a modified dressing, 
1 1/2 cups good mayonnaise
1/4 to 1/2 cup sweet white wine (to taste, instead of sugar)
3 tablespoon Dijon mustard
3 tablespoons whole-grain mustard
2 tablespoons minced fresh tarragon leaves

Like other reviewers, I omitted the sugar and added some cooked chicken (previously seasoned with Creole seasoning). My husband loves this but I couldn't stand his mom's recipe. Added this one to the books--its the first time I've gone back for seconds!
I added extra basil and omitted the celery only because I forgot to buy some. I added black pepper. It is FANTASTIC. Best pasta salad I have ever made. 😁

Really Really good! I cooked the broccoli (Next time I will throw it in with the pasta the last few minutes) and since I didn't have green peppers (or red or orange) or green onions I added half an onion and some carrots for color. I haven't served it yet but I tried it and am sure my family will love it.

Delicious basic recipe. Here's how I did it: I cooked the broccoli with the pasta (my family likes their broccoli soft- if yours doesn't, don't add broccoli until the last 5 minutes of cooking time). 2 c. Hellman's Light olive oil mayo, no onions (didn't have any) and added 1/4 tsp of onion powder & 1/4 tsp garlic salt to the mayo mix. I sauteed some chicken strips in a little olive oil, then added a splash of white wine. I then added the pasta/broccoli to the large bowl I had made the mayo mixture in, and added in the chicken. I had tasted the mayo mix before I added the pasta, & it was a little too bland. This was really good, but I felt like it was missing something, I can't put my finger on it. Still, very good and will make it again.

Fearing it might be too sweet for my guests, I cut back alittle on the Miracle Whip replacing with Hidden Valley Ranch dressing. I used about 3/4 of the red pepper since I love them. I also added a jar of drained marinated articoke hearts. It was a huge success at my pool party.

I was looking for a pasta salad that was different from the ones that are always at cookouts. This one had great reviews so I decided to give it a try. Wow! Everyone at the party loved it! I made a few changes. Used one orange pepper instead of 1/2 green and 1/2 red. I wanted to add more color. I increased the basil to 2 teaspoons. Other than that everything else was the same. The sugar was a really nice touch to add some sweetness to the miracle whip. This recipe is a keeper!!
I make this recipe for my fiancee's family a fee times a year. They absolutely love it I usually triple the recipe because her father always wants to have some to take home.

I can not tell you enough how good this pasta was! I made it exactly as the recipe said minus the green onions simply because I didn’t have any on hand and it was so good. Would be perfect for a summer picnic. My new go to pasta salad from now on!
I made this pasta salad and it was Deelish!

I left out the green peppers. I don't think it made a big difference. I took it to a baby shower for a couple having twins and decorating the nursery in Dr Who theme. The bow ties went well with that theme! It was a big hit! The sauce makes it delicious!
Absolutely delicious
This was good but a touch bland in flavor. I added 1/4 teaspoon paprika.
I cut the sugar in half. Still too sweet for my liking but no complaints from the rest of the crowd. I will make it again and cut the sugar even more.

great salad! well receieved! I made for a large family function and I got lots of compliments and several requests for the recipe! I made it the night before and it was served for lunch and it was great.
I kept the recipe just how it was... i'll be making this one again!
Made it exactly as written but halved it for just hubby and me. Delicious!
